Pagination is applied to the full run list, then those runs are grouped into projects. I’ll confirm that against the current page and API so the explanation matches what you see.

Pagination covers every run, across all projects. It does not page inside a project card.

All of your runs are sorted newest first, then cut into pages of 5. The runs on that page are grouped into project cards afterward. The control under the list moves through that combined history, so the count is “1–5 of all runs,” not “1–5 of this project.”

A card can therefore show only the slice of that project that landed on the current page. The rest of its runs show up on another page, sometimes in a second card for the same repository.

Putting the pager inside each card would keep a project’s runs together and let you page that project on its own. The page would list every project, and only a long card would get its own pages. That matches the cards better than one timeline split across projects.

so if current project has 10 runs and old one has 5 what would happen to the pagination?

With the current project at 10 runs and an old project at 5, you get 15 runs and 3 pages of 5. Which card appears on a page depends on when those runs were created, because pages are cut from one newest-first list before the cards are built.

**The current project’s 10 runs are the newest.** Page 1 is a Current card with the 5 newest runs. Page 2 is another Current card with the other 5. Page 3 is the Disconnected card with all 5 old runs.

**The old project’s 5 runs are the newest.** Page 1 is only the Disconnected card. The Current card is missing until page 2, then page 3 shows the rest of its runs. The “no runs for this project yet” line stays hidden, because those 10 runs exist on later pages.

**The two projects are mixed in time.** A page can hold both cards, each with only the runs that fell on that page. Five current and two old on the same page becomes a Current card with 5 runs and a Disconnected card with 2. The Current card is placed first on that page even when some of the old runs are newer.

A few other shapes of the same list:

- **6 current runs and no old ones.** Two pages, and both pages are the same Current card, split 5 then 1.
- **4 current and 1 old, 5 runs total.** One page, both cards, and the pager stays hidden because everything fits.
- **0 current and 5 old.** One Disconnected card, and the “no runs for this project yet” line shows above it.
- **You are on a page that has none of the current project’s runs.** That page shows only the old card. The in-progress lock and the latest saved numbers still come from the full history, so those stay correct on every page.

With a page size of 5, your 10 current runs and 5 old runs make 15 runs and 3 pages. Runs are ordered newest first across both projects, then cut into those pages. Each page is grouped into cards afterward, and the current project’s card is placed first on that page.

If the current project’s runs are the newer ones, which is the usual case after a reconnect:

- **Page 1** shows the 5 newest current runs, in one Current card. The old project is not on this page.
- **Page 2** shows the other 5 current runs, again in one Current card.
- **Page 3** shows the 5 old runs, in one Disconnected card.

The control reads “1–5 of 15,” then “6–10 of 15,” then “11–15 of 15.” A card only lists the runs that landed on that page, so the current project’s 10 runs never appear together.

If the timestamps are mixed, one page can hold runs from both projects. That page shows two cards, and each card lists only its runs from that page. The same repository can appear again on the next page with the rest of its runs.

A few other shapes:

- **5 or fewer runs in total** leaves the pager hidden.
- **4 current and 2 old, current newer:** page 1 has both cards (4 current, 1 old). Page 2 is a Disconnected card with the last old run.
- **No current runs and 5 old ones:** one Disconnected card, plus the “no runs for this project yet” line. No pager.
- **10 current runs and no old project:** two pages, only the Current card, 5 runs each.
- **A run still in progress** keeps the Start button locked even when that run is on another page.
